title: Korea Stock Market Today, Nov 2, 2026: KOSPI +2.24%, KOSDAQ +1.38% as Chip Exports Lift Large Caps
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,859.08, up 2.24%, and KOSDAQ closed at 734.36, up 1.38%, as better-than-feared October chip export data and institutional buying lifted large chip stocks after a weak start. Individual themes moved on their own news: AI server substrate makers, Hyundai Motor Group affiliates after third-quarter results, chip equipment and display equipment names, robotics, shipbuilding stocks on a U.S. Navy amphibious ship contract, and HLB Group companies.

1. Large chip stocks rebound — export data and institutional buying

Early in the session, large chip stocks were weak after Intel's sharp fall in the U.S. and worries about the profitability of AI investment. Sentiment recovered when October chip export figures came in solid, and buying by institutions and pension funds led a rebound in Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. KOSPI closed at 5,859.08 (+2.24%) and KOSDAQ at 734.36 (+1.38%).

Samsung Electronics and SK hynix drew dip buying on the export data and a sense that the earlier drop had gone too far; SK hynix was also reportedly supported by flows tied to its share buyback. SK Square, a holding company that owns SK hynix shares, rose together with it as sentiment improved.

2. AI servers and chip PCBs — demand for high-value substrates

With AI accelerator and data center investment continuing, makers of high-layer PCBs and memory substrates strengthened.

  • Isu Petasys: drew attention on news that it has started initial mass production of baseboards for next-generation AI accelerators. It is also reported to be developing and producing substrates for NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin platform, PCBs for a Google-related OAM accelerator and substrates for 1600G switches.
  • Simmtech: makes PCBs for memory modules and package substrates, and expectations rose for demand for substrates for AI server SOCAMM modules and high-value BT substrates. Brokerages' forecasts of better third-quarter results also appeared to affect sentiment; these are estimates, not confirmed results.
  • Korea Circuit: its high-value package substrate business, including FC-BGA that connects CPUs and GPUs to servers, was tied to expectations of more AI server investment.
  • TLB: expectations for memory module PCBs and substrates for next-generation SOCAMM were reflected.

3. Hyundai Motor Group — robot business expansion and third-quarter results

Hyundai Motor Group affiliates drew attention for better auto parts earnings, expansion of the robot business and expectations for AI infrastructure investment.

  • Hyundai Mobis: third-quarter operating profit was 914.1 billion won, up 17.2% from a year earlier, driven by a recovery in the European EV market and higher sales of core parts. News that it will begin producing actuator prototypes for Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot from November was also seen as positive.
  • Hyundai AutoEver: drew attention for investing 114.6 billion won in a Saemangeum AI data center joint venture to hold a 26% stake, tied to growth in GPU-as-a-service and AI infrastructure. Its third-quarter operating profit fell 2.6% from a year earlier, so its results themselves were not a positive.
  • Hyundai Glovis: third-quarter revenue of 9.0536 trillion won and operating profit of 566.5 billion won were its highest quarterly results ever, helped by growth in shipping and logistics, more non-affiliate customers and a favorable freight environment.

4. Chip equipment, system chips and displays

  • Wirt: supplies cleanroom equipment such as temperature and humidity control for chip processes and was grouped into the theme on hopes of a recovery in chip capital spending. As of 10:40 a.m. it was up about 0.66%, so no strong stock-specific catalyst was confirmed.
  • Coasia: works in system chip design and ASICs, and a recovery in sentiment toward AI chip and system chip stocks seems to have helped. No new order or disclosure was confirmed that day, so it is better read as theme-driven buying.
  • Viatron: signed a roughly 26.2 billion won display manufacturing equipment supply contract with China's MINYANG HKC. The contract equals about 40.2% of its 2025 revenue, and a 20% down payment was received, according to the disclosure. This is a concrete stock-specific catalyst.

5. Robotics and automation — rehab robots, wafer transfer robots and plant expansion

  • PNS Robotics: expanded from gait rehabilitation robots to a shoulder rehabilitation robot, secured hospital supply in Korea and EU CE MDR certification, and has a record of an additional 2.56 billion won supply contract with a rehabilitation center in Mexico. It plans to unveil a new product prototype at CES 2027.
  • Raon Robotics: preliminary third-quarter revenue was 26.5 billion won, up 104.7% from a year earlier, and operating profit was 3.9 billion won, up 259.3%. As a maker of semiconductor wafer transfer robots, its results and hopes for a chip cycle recovery were reflected.
  • Wonik Holdings: holds about 96% of Wonik Robotics, which works in robot hands and autonomous robots, and expectations for outside investment and robot business expansion at Wonik Robotics may act as a catalyst. No new individual order was announced that day.
  • Zenix Robotics: disclosed on October 30 that it will buy land and a building in Cheonan for 7.8 billion won to secure an automation equipment factory, raising expectations for expanded production and research space.

6. U.S. Navy ship building — hopes for Korea-U.S. shipbuilding cooperation

Shipbuilding and marine parts stocks strengthened on news that a Korean-owned company was selected for the first time as a builder in a U.S. Navy medium landing ship program.

Hanwha Defense USA, the U.S. subsidiary of Hanwha Aerospace, secured a contract worth $269 million from TOTE Services of the U.S. to build one medium landing ship, with an option for three more. Because the order goes through a local shipyard in Philadelphia, hopes grew for expansion of MASGA, the Korea-U.S. shipbuilding cooperation project.

  • Hanwha Ocean, Hanwha Engine and Hanwha Systems: rose together on hopes of Hanwha Group's entry into the U.S. naval ship market and expansion of local shipyard business.
  • HD Hyundai Marine Engine: benefited from shipbuilding hopes, a license agreement with global ship engine maker WinGD and a 197.2% rise in third-quarter operating profit.
  • Hyundai Hims: a ship block and shipbuilding parts maker that rose on expectations of more orders across the industry.

The contracting party for this deal is Hanwha Defense USA. Hanwha Ocean, Hanwha Engine and Hanwha Systems did not directly win this ship contract; they rose on group and shipbuilding supply chain expectations.

7. HLB Group — FDA review hopes and HLB Pharma product sales

  • HLB Pharma: its exclusively distributed New Zealand ghee, "Milkio Gold," sold out in 20 minutes in its first CJ Home Shopping broadcast. A total of 17,704 bottles were sold for about 410 million won in sales, and plans to widen sales channels were announced.
  • HLB Global and HLB Therapeutics: sentiment toward the group appears to have been affected by expectations that the FDA's review classification for the resubmitted liver cancer combination therapy of rivoceranib and camrelizumab will come in early November.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 2?
KOSPI rose 2.24% to 5,859.08 and KOSDAQ rose 1.38% to 734.36. Chip stocks were weak early but recovered after October export data was solid.

Did Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Systems win the U.S. Navy ship order?
No. The contracting party for the one medium landing ship is Hanwha Defense USA. The other Hanwha affiliates rose on group and shipbuilding supply chain expectations.

Are Simmtech's third-quarter results confirmed?
No. Brokerages' forecasts of better third-quarter results affected sentiment, but forecasts are not confirmed results.

This brief is our own summary based on same-day Korean market coverage and Daum Finance closing data; it is not a translation and not investment advice. See our Disclaimer and evidence labels.
